source.title: Towards Understanding Normalization in Neural ODEs
source.authors: Julia Gusak; L. Markeeva; T. Daulbaev; Alexandr M. Katrutsa; A. Cichocki; I. Oseledets

record.tranche_reason: The study compares normalization choices in neural ODEs, but reports test accuracy and solver-dependent inference behavior, not the training error, convergence speed, or learning-rate tolerance measured by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported CIFAR-10 test-accuracy comparisons are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Cited claims about batch normalization from prior work are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study measures final test accuracy and solver-dependent smoothness of neural ODE dynamics. It reports no training-error, training-speed, learning-rate-tolerance, initialization, width, or depth comparison that tests V1–V6. Its statements about batch normalization accelerating training cite prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that normalization and training solver affect final model performance and inferred smoothness of hidden-representation dynamics; models with similar test accuracy can differ substantially in that smoothness.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains neural ODE image classifiers and compares normalization schemes; it does not reproduce the training-error, width, depth, initialization, stability, or speed tests in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with ODE-block normalization; inferred smoothness also varies with normalization and training solver settings.

fits_no_version.finding: ODENet10 final CIFAR-10 test accuracy depends on normalization placement: ODE-block BN gives 76.2%, whereas other ODE-block choices give 92.5–93.0% with BN retained elsewhere. Standard ResNet10 gives 93.1%. Removing BN from the best model gives 91.2%; a fully unnormalized model gives 92%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice and placement affect final test accuracy in the tested neural ODE classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: ODENet4 inference accuracy responds differently to stronger evaluation solvers depending on training solver and normalization. Under the authors' smoothness criterion, BN-LN passes with 16 training steps, while BN-WN requires 32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training solver and normalization affect solver-dependent smoothness of learned neural ODE dynamics.

record.problems: The reported accuracy values are test accuracy, not training error or training-speed measurements. The smoothness criterion is described by the authors as limited because it requires the IVP solution to be Lipschitz in parameters and inputs.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 includes solver-dependent test-accuracy curves for ODENet4, but precise values are figure-only and the stated examples concern smooth-dynamics classification rather than any claim version; not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including clean or corrupted labels, model-size dependence, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and additional student width.
Depth-related training degradation, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature changes, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Faster accuracy gains, tolerance of higher learning rates, and Fixup training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 findings are already declared in rows_left_out. Its smoothness criterion concerns hidden-representation dynamics, not loss-surface smoothness or faster optimization. No verdict on V6 follows from the poor final accuracy with ODE-block BN.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, model size, and effects of early stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and the effect of student width.
Depth-related training error in plain versus residual networks, and the stated special-initialization or normalization-free exceptions.
Initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training behavior above stability limits, including curvature, sharpness, low training loss, and divergence.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates, and whether Fixup enables normalization-free residual training.
